answer: Each new identity is tied to one network vantage: before its first vote counts, the node must answer a latency probe from the same point of presence within 120 milliseconds on seven consecutive days. Influence stays at zero until the streak hits its zenith on day seven, so flooding early earns nothing and rented cloud footprints cannot forge the timing profile. A tundra server still sits too far from the probe to make the window. Each fake identity pays a week of colocation and bandwidth in one region, about 30 dollars per head; an honest agent's ordinary week already satisfies it.
